_comment: Acceptance probes for scripts/check_routing_acceptance.py.
Each case asserts a package is reachable on BOTH retrieval surfaces:
must_carry -> terms that must survive the 220-char gloss clip (surface 1, ships)
probes     -> phrasings that must rank it in top_n (surface 2, local index)
These are acceptance tests for specific packages, NOT a benchmark. They do not
belong in evals/measurement/heldout-queries.json: those 154 queries are a fixed,
hand-written measurement set, and adding queries whose answers were authored in
the same wave would inflate the number it reports.
WHY THESE PACKAGES. Before the 2026-08-15 record-access wave the corpus had no
package for restriction rules, scoping rules, sharing rules, the role hierarchy,
or permission-set expiration, and these queries misrouted:
'create a scoping rule'             -> apex/soql-using-scope-clause (the SOQL
clause: a different feature sharing a word)
'criteria based sharing rule'       -> data/sharing-recalculation-performance
'design the role hierarchy'         -> admin/territory-design-requirements
'configure a lightning record page' -> agentforce/einstein-prediction-builder
'set up single sign on with saml'   -> security/sso-saml-troubleshooting, i.e.
troubleshooting, with no setup package
KNOWN LIMITATION, deliberately not papered over. Probes here are specific
phrasings. Abstract paraphrases still miss on the lexical surface -- e.g.
'default record scope without removing access' returns admin/user-management, and
'which lightning record page does a user see' returns admin/dynamic-forms-migration,
even though both packages own those topics and carry near-identical trigger
sentences. That is the corpus-wide natural-language weakness the held-out
benchmark reports (Hit@1 ~40%), not a defect in these packages. Do NOT 'fix' it by
pasting probe strings verbatim into the triggers: array -- that makes this file
measure its own echo. Probes and triggers are kept as paraphrases on purpose.
